name: the detector counts the blocks the transport will drop
comment: The predicate itself. Bound to the request SHAPE rather than to the SDK's warning string, so this is the anchor that would rot if the SDK reshaped a message — which is exactly what the contract test exists to say out loud.
old:
total += sum(
            1 for block in content
            if isinstance(block, dict) and REASONING_BLOCK_KEY in block
        )

name: a pass another hook cancelled is not an opportunity
comment: The pass ReplyGuard refuses is never formatted, so it strips nothing — and on the tag path it is MOST turns, with a reasoning block sitting in agent.messages at exactly that moment.
old:
if event.cancel:
                # Another hook already refused this pass (see the class
                # docstring). Nothing will be formatted, so nothing is stripped.
                self._pending = None
                return

name: the watch registers AFTER the guard, so it sees event.cancel
comment: BeforeModelCallEvent dispatches in registration order. Registered first, the watch reads a cancel flag nobody has set yet and counts the refused pass — the same defect as the entry above, reached through the wiring instead of through the code.
old:
if reasoning_watch is not None:
        hooks.append(reasoning_watch)
new:
if reasoning_watch is not None:
        hooks.insert(0, reasoning_watch)

name: one position asked twice is one opportunity
old:
if depth <= self._last_depth:
                # The same position, asked twice. Counted once: the ratio is
                # strips per opportunity in the conversation, not per HTTP
                # request.
                return

name: a model call that raised settles nothing
comment: BeforeModelCallEvent fires INSIDE the retry loop, so an attempt that throttled is the same position re-entered. The first sweep found this GREEN against the retry test: a retry lands on the same depth either way, so the depth guard masked it and the totals agreed. The target is now the pass that raised and was NOT retried, where the two guards disagree - that one would otherwise put a `stripped` on a request nobody got an answer from.
old:
if getattr(event, "exception", None) is not None:
                return

name: a stripped continuation call is counted
stripped_blocks is DISTINCT reasoning lost, not re-drops of it
comment: The message list only grows, so a running sum counts the first pass's block once per later request and reports more reasoning lost than the turn ever produced.

name: the DENOMINATOR is recorded
comment: The one that makes this a measurement rather than a tally: without continuation_calls there is nothing to divide by, and 2-of-2 and 2-of-200 are the same row.

name: the counter carries its own denominator too
comment: A numerator-only series cannot separate «no strips» from «no observation» — both read as absent, and this process restarts two or three times a day with labels created lazily.

name: a turn with no opportunity leaves no row
flush is idempotent
comment: Both production paths flush from more than one exit and the Dreamer from three, so a second call must not be a second row.

name: a failed write is counted, never raised into the turn
old:
await asyncio.wait_for(
                self._store.record_observation(observation),
                timeout=self._write_timeout_seconds,
            )
            outcome = "ok"
        except Exception:
            log.exception("ReasoningStripWatch write failed; ignoring")
new:
await asyncio.wait_for(
                self._store.record_observation(observation),
                timeout=self._write_timeout_seconds,
            )
            outcome = "ok"
        except ValueError:
            log.exception("ReasoningStripWatch write failed; ignoring")

name: provenance is read off the model that made the call
comment: Config says what was configured; the row says what was SENT. That distinction is the whole reason the 2026-09-17 combo change took two hours to reconstruct.

name: the invoke stage flushes the watch
comment: The line that turns a counted turn into a STORED one on the tag and participation paths — the half a Prometheus counter cannot give across a restart.
old:
if reasoning_watch is not None:
        await reasoning_watch.flush()

name: the delivery handle labels the path with the audience
the Dreamer flushes its watch
the Dreamer's rows name the ADAPTOR
comment: One run a day per adaptor, so «dreamer» alone is the wrong grain for the question «which path».

name: the database refuses a row with no opportunity
comment: The second lock on the same property as the `observation` entry above. The first one is a writer, and a writer is what drifts.

name: a naive created_at is refused before it reaches timestamptz
comment: created_at is the column an operator groups by to ask «did this move when the model did». A naive value is stored under the session timezone — a real instant, silently the wrong one.

name: THE BLOCKER: the row write is BOUNDED inside the held slot
comment: Round four of a defect this repo has fixed twice. A wedged Postgres does not raise — it does not ANSWER — so `except Exception` is no defence and the conversation's slot is held until the await returns. The target's own outer `wait_for` is what makes this RED rather than a hang, which would stop the sweep instead of reporting on it.

name: the architecture control can SEE the reasoning-strip write
comment: The half that stops a fifth instance. The gate walked one module and its docstring claimed that module held the only unbounded slot-held await in the repo; this PR's first draft falsified the sentence and the gate stayed green. Dropping the registry entry must redden the control's own positive control, not the bounded-ness assertion.

name: an unreadable provenance never overwrites a readable one
comment: R-27 applied to provenance. `_model_identity` answers ('', '') for four distinct conditions; overwriting unconditionally let a transient read failure on the LAST call erase a good read from the first.

name: an impossible row is refused under its own name, not as `failed`
comment: `failed` is also what a database blip gives. Letting the CHECK refuse it instead surfaces as an IntegrityError counted `failed` — the one confusion this outcome exists to end.

name: a turn with no opportunity moves no write counter
comment: Without this the `finally` records `failed` for every single-call turn in the system, on the one series that says the record has gone blind.

name: the write counter is recorded on every exit, guarded
comment: `flush` runs PAST the stage's own `except`, so an exception from `Metrics.inc` (KeyError on an undeclared name) lands on a turn that was supposed to be costless. The mutation removes the recording entirely.

name: `path`'s vocabulary is DERIVED, so heartbeat and proactive are in it
comment: First sweep found this GREEN against a test parametrized over SPEAKING_AUDIENCES itself -- shrinking the set shrank the test with it, which is a target that can only agree with whatever the code says. The target is now the call-site walk: narrow the Literal and `fire.py` is passing values the declaration no longer contains.

name: the tag path passes the NAMED audience, not a literal
comment: Also GREEN first time round, against a test that called `deliver.build` with its own audiences and so could not see what the pipeline passes. The call-site walk resolves the real expression and refuses a value the declaration does not carry.

name: the budget-exhaustion draft is counted into the same row
comment: A DECISION rather than an accident: the draft is a second `invoke_async` whose request carries the accumulated reasoning and genuinely loses it. The mutation flushes before the draft can run, which is what excluding it would look like.
old:
if reasoning_watch is not None:
        await reasoning_watch.flush()
new:
if reasoning_watch is not None:
        reasoning_watch._model_calls = min(reasoning_watch._model_calls, 2)
        reasoning_watch._continuation_calls = min(
            reasoning_watch._continuation_calls, 1)
        reasoning_watch._strip_calls = min(reasoning_watch._strip_calls, 1)
        await reasoning_watch.flush()
